parts:
Following the lead of this thread: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/shiny-discuss/multi$20page/shiny-discuss/yWEQuofjsdA/pnH6wW4s_SkJ

I built a pared down version of a multi page app found here: https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radiant

I can get ggplot, tags, markdown, etc. to render fine in my app, but ggvis, according to the example, doesn't work.

Thanks in advance - I really love working with Shiny, but have been out for a while - I have effectively zero experience with ggvis, just trying to follow examples.

Here's a non-working example of what I'm doing. I can post the full thing later if needed.

# server.R
library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(ggvis)
library(dplyr)
library(reshape2)

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  observe({
    if(input$tool == 'email'){
      for(f in list.files('email', pattern = '*.(R|r)$', full.names = TRUE)) 
        source(f, local=TRUE) ## sourcing the 'email' folder
    }
  })
  
})

# ui.R
## "nav" and "tabs" are functions that recursively go through a ui navigation structure.
shinyUI(
  bootstrapPage(
    tags$head(tags$link(rel='stylesheet', type='text/css', href='css/style.css')),
    nav(menus, id='tool', brand='email'),
    fluidRow(column(width=10, 
      tabs(menus, id='tabs', brand='email'),
      offset = 1
      )
    ),
    title = "Voleris campaigns"
  )
)

# when the user clicks the "email" tab (called so because it shows the results of an email campaign, not because it sends email)
# the below ui is created 
#  tabPanel("Email", id='email', column(width = 12,
#   uiOutput("ui_email"),
#  uiOutput("route_options")
#    )
#  ),

# server code above will find this file.
# email.R 
data <- readRDS('email/data/email.rds')
output$ui_email <- renderUI({
    column(width = 6, 
           h1('Email campaign analysis'),
           h4(sprintf("Date range: %s - %s", 
                     strftime(data$startdate[1], "%b. %d '%y"),
                     strftime(data$enddate[1], "%b. %d '%y"))),
           hr(),
           includeMarkdown("email/md/email.md")
           ## for some reason, this causes a warning
           ## when attempting to include a ggvis plot, runs fine without it.
           ##incomplete final line found on 'email/md/email.md'
           )
})

output$route_options <- renderUI({
  column(width = 6, 
    h4('Top level results'),
    selectInput("route", "", selectList(as.character(data$route)),
                selected = "HMO-TIJ",
                width='20%'),
    column(width=6, 
      h4('Total sales by route'), offset=1
    ),
    plotOutput('total_sales'), ## works fine
    ggvisOutput('ggvis_total_sales'),  ## causes error
    class = 'pad-top'
  )
})

output$total_sales <- renderPlot({
  data %>% 
    filter(as.character(route) == input$route) %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x=communication, y=total_sales)) + geom_bar(stat='identity') + 
    theme_bw() + 
    xlab('') + ylab('') +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar)
})
ggvis_total_sales <- renderPlot({
  data %>% 
    filter(as.character(route) == input$route) %>% 
    ggviz(prop('x', communication), prop('y', total_sales)) %>% layer_bars()
})

## including this line throws the following warning - called a warning, but the ui does not render - gray screen
## Unhandled error in observer: bind_shiny requires a ggvis object or a reactive expression that returns a ggvis object
ggvis_total_sales %>% bind_shiny('ggvis_total_sales')

I guess it should be ggvis and not ggviz. I didn't test if that solves the issue.
